What did we include, and where did it come from?
    19 claims stand behind this building, and every one of
      them is in exactly one row here. The tables further down carry them one at a time, with
      the reasoning behind why; the decisions that belong to no single claim are under
      “Liberties taken here”.

    Where did it stand?
    
      
    recorded position
    Beside the log jail at northwest public square, facing Randolph; exact position reconstructed.reconstructed
    Reconstructed house southwest corner7.8m east of the jail's preceding southwest convention, and1.30m north of the core's new reconstructed access setback; both face north by convention. This east registration gives the Gale view's keeper-left/compound-right order. Neither7.8m spacing,1.30m offset, compass registration nor exact setback is surveyed or measured from the print. House and core remain in the public square; current terrain and doorway clearance require actual published app review. No street or parcel control moves.
    why
  
    
  
      
    Was it inside the town's fire limit?
    Inside the limit — hay could not lawfully be stacked here.
    Section 22 of the by-laws the Trustees passed on
      5 August 1835 made it unlawful to stack hay inside a boundary they walked street
      by street — 198.9 acres
      of it — under twenty-five dollars a stack. It is the town's own statement of where
      it was built up closely enough to burn, five weeks after this scene.
    commencing on Washington street, at the United States Reservation, and running thence West to the intersection of Canal Street, thence North to the intersection of Kinzie Street, thence East to the intersection of Wolcott street, thence to Illinois Street, and thence to Lake Michigan
    The Chicago Democrat, 19 August 1835, page 1 —
      the limit is derived from committed street lines, never drawn in the scene.

    1inferred
    sources: Cook County’s First Jail as it was in 1836…One brick-looking stack appears in Gale. The corrected pictured-end assignment moves the same reconstructed prototype stack to localu5.5m near the east pictured gable; neither location nor dimensions are source measurements.

    function
    dwellinginferred
    sources: Cook County’s First Jail as it was in 1836…Gale 1902 p51 places John Beach in a house beside the jail, facing Randolph, and a house is a dwelling. INFERRED and not documented, deliberately: Trowbridge's plate and Gale's recollection are a modern reconstruction pictorial and retrospective sources, and the project's evidence ladder forbids a documented value resting on a modern reconstruction alone, so the use is read off a memoir rather than attested by a period record. Who the household was beyond Beach, when the house went up and came down, where exactly it stood and every dimension of it are reconstruction, recorded on the phase and in the liberties register under “the keeper dwelling and low compound gate”.

    sources: Cook County’s First Jail as it was in 1836…One corrected north-facing interpretation of the1902 Gale artwork captioned1836: depicted gable is the model east/uMax end; local-u D/W/W stations read W/W/D from outside the north front, with two depicted gable ground sash and loft light. All numeric set-out, compass registration and July1835 continuity remain reconstructed. Andreas has a different elevation; no reconciliation or match is claimed.
    why
  
    plan
    hall parlourreconstructed
    Native base plan vocabulary only; interior rooms are unknown. The opt-in picture layout governs front apertures.

    porch
    —reconstructed
    No roofed porch is asserted. The opt-in layout draws the pictured low front rail with a clear door station; a separate native enclosure supplies the low hung compound gate. A historically measured landing/platform is not known.
    why
  
    roof pitch deg
    25reconstructed
    One finite low-gable prototype; no source measures angle.

    greenreconstructed
    Dark open shutters appear at pictured windows. The actual hue/material detail is not shown in monochrome; native green is reconstructed.
    why
  
    siding exposure (m)
    0.152reconstructed
    INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this record wears 6 in — dealt by the siding stock generator: keyed to the phase's construction season, because buildings sided from the same season's shipments of St Joseph sawn lumber tend toward one stock, then advanced so no frame building within 60 m shares this one's. The separation is the surface variety other work reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. the liberties register “Every named frame building's siding stock is dealt, not found” owns the invention.
    why

    One low main storey plus a small unclassified loft light; no habitable half storey asserted.
    why

    Prototype standing height, not measured from drawing.

    what this source supplies, and does not

    supplies

    • Independently verified1902 publication and named book illustrator for the exact detailed jail artwork.
    • Visible core/keeper-house/palisade composition, gabled log core and upright barred-looking gable opening in the captioned1836depiction.
    • Gale p51’s retrospective prose about the palisade and John Beach’s partly enclosed house, with narrative date limits.

    does not supply

    • A resolved original-cell/later-cell construction sequence or reconciliation with the Andreas hip-roof depiction.
